clue.text: Brother and officer becoming target for cowboys?

parts.note: BRO is the informal short form of brother
NCO is a non-commissioned officer, such as a sergeant

explanation.surface: A sibling and a sergeant are both turning into figures the cowboys want to shoot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Target' is not something to aim at but something to ride and break in, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an untamed horse that rodeo riders try to stay on, so it is literally what they set out to master.

clue.text: Decay restricting a second joint

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: rot is decay
taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Rot has set in and is limiting movement in a second joint of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as a body part beside 'decay', but it is a cut of meat for the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of beef or lamb cooked in the oven is called a roast, as in the Sunday roast.

clue.text: Not recording a person in facility for making records

parts.note: taken as written
an EP (extended play) is a short record
taken as written
per. is a dictionary abbreviation for person

explanation.surface: Someone is refusing to record a person in a studio built for making records.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'records' in the definition are written notes, not discs, despite the recording talk beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is the material that lets you jot down written notes and messages, a means for keeping written records.

clue.text: Weber opera opening in Oslo, with live run being broadcast

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of the city is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the city name
to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a run said in a broad accent, close to the man's name Ron

explanation.surface: A Weber opera premieres in Oslo and its live run is broadcast on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match of run with RON is loose, needing a short vowel some accents give it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber wrote the 1826 opera named after the fairy king from A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Success securing new home at the outset — that is a good feeling

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a boom is a period of success
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so just the first letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of home
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Finally getting a new house brings a warm feeling of contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOM opens between its two Os to take in the N and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful friendliness and goodwill, a warm genial disposition towards other people.

clue.text: This end of the bench needs to be repaired covertly

indicators.note: something needing repair must be put back together, so its letters are rebuilt in a fresh order
the end of a word is its tail, so only its final letters are used

parts.note: the last two letters of this
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: One end of a workbench is broken and must be fixed quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs' is part of the letters to be shuffled as well as holding up the surface sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done out of public view, as stagehands work out of the audience's sight, is done secretly or covertly.

clue.text: High-level person goes white when cornered by indication of former name

indicators.note: cornered means hemmed in on both sides, so one piece is surrounded by the other

parts.note: née marks a woman's maiden name
someone who goes white pales

explanation.surface: A senior figure blanches when confronted about a previous name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-level' sounds like rank, but it means living high up, in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal sits in the Himalayas, home of the highest peaks, so its people live at great altitude.

clue.text: Gems having phosphorus as well, but oxygen primarily

indicators.note: having means holding, so one letter is placed inside the other piece
primarily means first, so the oxygen letter is moved to the front of its word

parts.note: also means as well
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: these gemstones contain phosphorus and also, chiefly, oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSO has its O brought to the front, then P is slipped in after that O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent precious stones, so they are examples of gems.

clue.text: Significance supported by article in French press

parts.note: import is significance or importance
une is the French feminine indefinite article

explanation.surface: An important matter is backed up by an article in the French newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the second piece below the first. 'Press' seems to be the newspapers but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune someone is to pester or urge them persistently, which is to press them hard.

clue.text: Marine vessel out of place in Tibet and next answer (with height being involved)

indicators.note: letters out of place are disordered, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to the following clue, 10 across
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A navy ship looks absurdly out of place among Tibet's mountains and the Swiss peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With height being involved' adds H to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a heavily armoured warship of a navy, a seagoing vessel.

clue.text: A recording's offering a view of Switzerland?

parts.note: taken as written
an LP is a long-playing record
the possessive ending kept as written

explanation.surface: A record seems to offer a panorama of Switzerland, perhaps on its sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the mountains themselves are what 'offer' the view.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range dominating Swiss scenery is what any picture of the country tends to show.

clue.text: Getting depressed after sulks recalled? Leave the top job

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second one in the answer
recalled means called back, so the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: pets are fits of sulking
someone feeling depressed is down

explanation.surface: A boss sinks into gloom after past tantrums are remembered, and decides to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: A pet is an old word for a fit of sulking, as in being in a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish a senior post or resign from office is the idiom for giving up a leading position.

clue.text: Temptation to snatch stone? It's the shininess

indicators.note: to snatch is to grab and hold, so one piece ends up held inside the other

parts.note: a lure is a temptation
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: The temptation to grab a jewel comes from its sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the gleam or sheen of a surface that reflects light, as in polished stone.

clue.text: Dropping a catch may be mine?

definitions.text: Dropping a catch may be mine?

parts.words: Dropping a catch may be mine?
parts.note: surface reading: a cricketer confessing the dropped catch may have been their fault; setter's reading: the answer names both a mistake and the cricket fielding position by the wicketkeeper, where catches are dropped

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slips are close fielders beside the wicketkeeper who take edged catches; the word also means a small error.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blunder is a slip, and the fielder at slip is the one most likely to make that error with a catch.

clue.text: Stop in road, head away from car, and listen

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a road
to stop is to end

indicators.note: with its head away the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver pulls up in the road, leans out of the car, and listens.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom meaning to pay attention to what someone says, to hear them out.

clue.text: A source of culinary pleasure, but dates should be chopped

indicators.note: chopping cuts things up and scatters them, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: dates are a delight, but they should be chopped first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a link between two halves of a recipe note, yet its letters go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue's sensory receptors detect flavour, so they are where enjoyment of food comes from.

clue.text: 17, when dancing, involves hard ballet move

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one letter is placed inside the other piece
dancing letters move about, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 17 down
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An interval piece, when danced, includes a demanding ballet step.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a jump in ballet where the dancer rapidly crosses the legs in the air, a classic dance step.

clue.text: Stage music opening, but cut short? Excellent, about time

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
something cut short loses its tail, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an entry is an opening or way in
ace means excellent
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A review of a show's opening number: short, but excellent, considering the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is a piece of music played between the acts of a theatrical performance.

clue.text: Transport access

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb stressed on the second syllable: to delight or enrapture
second meaning, a noun stressed on the first syllable: a way in

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like travel words; the first is the sense of carrying someone away with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to fill with wonder, carrying someone away emotionally, while an entrance is a door or way in.

clue.text: Row after middle of kitchen device lost

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of the word as the one taken away
lost means gone, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a timer counts down the cooking

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out after the kitchen gadget goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of several levels or rows placed one above another, as in theatre seating.

clue.text: New face at court getting knight upset? Rubbish

parts.note: a deb (debutante) was a young woman presented at the royal court

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Sir is a knight's title

explanation.surface: A debutante upsets a knight at court; someone dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubble and waste left over, so it is a kind of rubbish.

clue.text: After reversing, drive into concrete food store

indicators.note: reversing runs things backwards, so the built word is read in the other direction
into means going inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: concrete means real, tangible
Dr is the street-name abbreviation for drive

explanation.surface: A driver backing up crashes into the concrete outside a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool pantry or cupboard where provisions are kept, a household store for food.

clue.text: Stand down protest over book

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stand down after protesting about a book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the protest above the book.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob, short for demobilise, is to release troops from military service, as a unit is stood down.

clue.text: Caught by the French soldiers, clearly heartless, but getting mercy

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
le is French for the
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

indicators.note: without its heart, the word keeps only its two outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of clearly

explanation.surface: Captured by French troops who are plainly heartless, yet somehow shown mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like a description of the soldiers but applies to the next word, clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Clemency is leniency shown to an offender, compassion that spares punishment, so it means mercy.

clue.text: Accommodation for fifteenth prisoner? It's a big fiddle!

parts.note: a cell houses a prisoner
O is the fifteenth letter of the alphabet
completes the phrase about housing an inmate; gives no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A cell for the fifteenth inmate? Someone cries that it is a huge swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prisoner' completes 'Accommodation for' and 'fiddle' sounds like fraud but means a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle is an informal word for violin, and the cello is a much larger member of the violin family.

clue.text: Better men to accept time in office?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the words hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Should more capable people be allowed a stint in government?
explanation.definitionFit: A term is the fixed period for which an official holds a post, such as a presidential term.

clue.text: Defender learnt he is out of place in soccer team after upset

indicators.note: after being upset the team abbreviation is turned round
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: FC stands for Football Club

indicators.note: letters out of place are disordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A defender discovers he is out of position in the side after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' only joins; 'upset' turns FC round.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre-half is a central defensive player in football, so the position is that of a defender.

clue.text: Dull style in clothing receiving unexpected ban

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: dress is clothing

indicators.note: unexpected suggests letters arriving in a surprising order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drab fashion look emerges from clothing hit by a surprise ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull style' is the definition; 'style' is not part of the clothing wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Drabness is dreariness or lack of colour, a dull, cheerless manner or appearance.

clue.text: Company in place beginning to make TV programme?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to place something is to sit it down

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of make
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A production company is in place to start making a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The company sits inside the place-plus-initial string, at the very join, so it reads like a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, short for situation comedy, is a type of television series, so it is one kind of show.
